slides.title: prompts to get a better deal on almost anything
slides.sub: Give it your leverage, get a script and a real number.
slides.voiceover: Here are five prompts that can get you a better deal on almost anything.

slides.name: The Rent Rescue
slides.sub: Turn a rent increase into a lower renewal offer.
slides.prompt: Act as an expert negotiator. My landlord wants to raise my rent from [CURRENT RENT] to [NEW RENT] at [ADDRESS]. My leverage is [ON-TIME PAYMENTS / CHEAPER COMPARABLES / LONG TENANCY]. Write a **POLITE COUNTER-OFFER**, a fallback ask if they refuse, and a realistic estimate of what I could save.
slides.tip: Send it in writing, not a phone call — a paper trail gives you room to negotiate again next year.
slides.voiceover: One. Turn a rent increase into a lower counter-offer, ready to send.

slides.name: The Used Car Closer
slides.sub: Walk into the lot with a number and a script.
slides.prompt: Act as an expert car negotiator. I'm buying a [YEAR/MAKE/MODEL] listed at [ASKING PRICE] with [MILEAGE/KNOWN ISSUES]. My leverage is [COMPARABLE LISTINGS / CASH OFFER / TIME ON THE LOT]. Give me a **TARGET PRICE**, an opening offer, a back-and-forth script, and a walk-away line.
slides.tip: Get three comparable listings ready before you go — specific numbers beat 'it feels expensive.'
slides.voiceover: Two. Walk into a car deal with a target price and a full script.

slides.name: The Retention Call Script
slides.sub: Get a discount before you even threaten to cancel.
slides.prompt: Act as an expert negotiator who worked in telecom retention. I want to lower my [INTERNET / PHONE / STREAMING] bill of [CURRENT PRICE] a month. My leverage is [COMPETITOR OFFER / YEARS AS A CUSTOMER]. Write a **STEP-BY-STEP CALL SCRIPT** ending in cancellation, plus a realistic estimate of the discount I could get.
slides.tip: Ask to be transferred to the 'retention department' by name — they can offer deals regular support can't.
slides.voiceover: Three. Get a retention discount before you even threaten to cancel.

slides.name: The Service Provider Reset
slides.sub: Cut a bill that just went up, without switching providers.
slides.prompt: Act as an expert negotiator. My [INSURANCE / GYM / SOFTWARE] plan costs [CURRENT PRICE] and just went up. My leverage is [X YEARS AS A CUSTOMER / A CHEAPER COMPETITOR QUOTE]. Write a short, firm message asking for a **RATE MATCH OR DISCOUNT**, plus a fallback ask if they say no.
slides.tip: Always ask 'is this the best you can do' one more time after their first answer — it often isn't.
slides.voiceover: Four. Ask any provider for a rate match, the polite but firm way.

slides.name: The Contractor Counter
slides.sub: Push back on a quote without losing the job.
slides.prompt: Act as an expert negotiator. A contractor quoted me [PRICE] for [JOB]. My leverage is [ANOTHER QUOTE / A FLEXIBLE TIMELINE]. Write a **RESPECTFUL COUNTER** asking for a lower price or added value, plus a realistic range of what I could save.
slides.tip: Get a second quote first — it's usually free, and it doubles your leverage in the first message.
slides.voiceover: Five. Push back on a contractor's quote without losing the job.

slides.title: Get more out of this pack
items: The more specific your leverage, the sharper the script — vague inputs get vague answers.
Read the AI's script back to yourself before the real call so it sounds like you.
The best negotiators are ready to leave — ask for one and actually mean it.
slides.voiceover: Fill in real numbers, practice the script out loud, and always have a walk-away line.
